note: Establish a complete baseline using five valuable blends plus C7, C8 and C9 products; subsequent tuning will target purity losses and column costs.
notebook:
PLAN: Build an 8-column full recovery skeleton (C4/C5 root; deethanize and split C3/C4; recover C5, C6 paraffin and C6 naphthene blends; split C7/C8/C9), then inspect purity and costs and optimize the weakest/most expensive columns. Step 1: baseline all 8.
Initial moderate stages/reflux, high pressure on light end to limit refrigeration, lower pressure downstream. Blend values dominate: estimated gross ~$3.2bn/yr. Ethane is low value but must be removed to sell C3 blend, and its own top must meet 95%.

note: Sharpen the root C4/C5 split before spending solves downstream; the current leakage prevents every major blend from meeting specification.
notebook:
PLAN: First make the root C4/C5 cut sharp enough to unlock the large C4 and C5 blend values, then add/tune downstream C5/C6 and C6/heavy splits; retain only profitable branches. Step 1: root cut optimization.
The 55-stage 2.5/2.5 root leaked 19% C5 overhead and butane into bottoms, so no product met spec. Moderate downstream columns cannot compensate for that poor feed split. Try 65 stages and 4/4 at 12-ish bar (dp .4): lower pressure improves relative volatility and warmer condenser avoids light-end refrigeration. Existing branch settings remain for a one-solve sensitivity test. Blend values dominate; prioritize C4/C5/C6 mixtures over pure heavy products.

note: Sharpen the two cuts controlling the valuable C5 and C6 blends, and eliminate the entire unprofitable heavy-product subtree.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a profitable blend backbone first: sharp C5/C6 root, C4/C5 split, C5 polishing and C6-paraffin/heavies split. Prune all low-margin heavy-product columns. Next tune only columns whose added revenue exceeds cost.
The existing root leaks about 150 mol/s C5 into B, while the current B split loses substantial C6 paraffins to BB. Use the proven R82 root (70 stages, reflux 3, boil-up 4, dp .45) and strengthen B to 65/3/4. Keep the successful T/TB C5 polishing sections. Selling BBB removes four heavy columns costing about $64M/yr whose products were all off spec. Target C5 + C6 blend revenue near $1.2B/yr before considering C3/C4 recovery.

note: Consolidate the two light columns into one stronger C4/C5 splitter and polish the high-value C6 paraffin blend, while pruning all off-spec heavy recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a profitable three-column blend backbone (C5/C6 root, C4/C5 split, C6-paraffin/heavies split), then tune cuts for >=95% purity and only add recovery columns with clear positive margin.
Current five-column design earns only $349M/yr and costs $597M/yr. The extra TB column is unnecessary: T already makes the required C4/C5 cut, so strengthening T should directly produce a saleable C5 blend. B currently makes a 90%-pure C6 paraffin blend worth about $1.08B/yr if polished; increasing its separation should recover that flagship revenue. Prune BB and all heavy recovery. Target roughly $1.5B/yr revenue with three columns, then reduce root/B duty and pressure costs after purity is secured.

note: Decisively strengthen both polishing columns to cross the 95% C5 and C6-paraffin blend specifications and establish revenue.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a profitable three-column blend backbone (C5/C6 root, C4/C5 split, C6-paraffin/heavies split), then tune cuts for >=95% purity and only add recovery columns with clear positive margin. Step: force first sales by sharply polishing T and B.
Current root already gives useful feeds: T outlet TB is 87% C5 (worth ~$619M/yr at spec) and B outlet BT is 93% C6 paraffin (worth ~$1.105B/yr at spec). Both are close, so a decisive increase in stages/reflux is justified despite cost. Heavy BB and light TT remain unsold. Once both blends sell, reduce expensive root severity and optimize polishing columns around the purity boundary. Other agents' milder columns remain off-spec, confirming that incremental tweaks are insufficient.

note: Sharpen the C4/C5 splitter decisively: recovering the $619M/yr C5 blend should outweigh the additional column cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a profitable three-column blend backbone, force C5 on-spec, then add only recovery columns with clear positive margin and finally trim excessive severity. Step: sharpen the C4/C5 splitter decisively.
Current root 70/3/4/.45, T 110/6/7/0 and B 110/6/7/.15 give reward .885. BT sells C6 paraffin for $1119M/y. TB is 88% C5 with 9% n-butane and is worth ~$619M/y once >=95%; this is the clearest large gain. TT has ~60% C4 and ~36% C3, so a future C3/C4 splitter may sell two blends. BB heavies are probably uneconomic to purify. Other agents' milder columns remain off-spec, confirming incremental tweaks are insufficient.

note: Adopt the proven C5/C6 plant and split its unsold light tops into C3 and C4 blends; both have large value and only ethane threatens the C3 specification.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the proven four-column C5/C6 backbone, monetise the C3/C4 stream, then improve C5 recovery and trim costs only where margins justify it. Step: split TT into saleable C3 and C4 blends.
Copy R314: its TB polisher gives $417M/y C5 revenue and reward 1.716. TT contains about 60% C4 and 36% C3 with only 4% ethane, so one moderately strong C3/C4 splitter should make both products meet their 95% blend specifications. Keep the profitable backbone unchanged while testing TT at 70 stages, reflux/boil-up 4/4 and no extra pressure drop.

note: Combine the best C5-recovery polisher with my proven C4-producing TT column; both improvements are independently profitable.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the best C5-recovery backbone, monetise the C4 stream with the proven TT splitter, then test C3 recovery and cheaper backbone settings. Step: combine R364 with the profitable C4 split.
R364's TB at 70/6/1.2 raises C5 revenue from $417M to $567M while cutting TB cost to $28.4M, giving 2.113. My TT at 70/4/4 sells the C4 blend for $149M at $50.9M cost, a clear net gain. Combining should give about 2.34 before further optimization. C3 tops remain only 80% C3 and are not yet saleable.

note: Sharpen the C3/C4 splitter to remove isobutane from the C3 tops while retaining the saleable C4 bottoms; this could unlock about $73M/yr of additional revenue.
notebook:

Current 2.337 uses TT 70/4/4: TTB sells C4 ($149M), but TTT is only 80% C3 with 10% ethane and 10% isobutane. Increasing TT stages/reflux should reject more isobutane to TTB and ethane overhead; the C3 blend is worth about $73M/yr. Backbone products are close to 95%, so avoid simultaneous backbone changes until the light split is established.

PLAN: Combine independently proven column-cost reductions, then test root savings and only pursue C3 if its extra recovery pays for another column. Step: merge R456's cheaper B column with R458's cheaper T column.
R456 gives 2.466 using B100/5/6 and T100/5/6. R458 proves T70/4/5 preserves both C5 and C6 products while saving about $52M/yr versus T110/6/7. These changes affect separate branches, so combining T70/4/5 with B100/5/6 should save about $80M/yr versus R456. TT110/8/4 was counterproductive: both light streams went off spec. Best TT remains 70/4/4; C3 recovery would also require ethane removal and is unlikely to justify much extra cost.

note: Reduce the expensive C6/heavy splitter while its blend has modest purity headroom; retain all other proven settings.
notebook:
PLAN: Reduce the two dominant column costs in measured steps while protecting the $1.109B C6 and $570M C5 sales; then test root savings and only pursue C3 if clearly profitable. Step: trial B80/4/5.
Best is 2.529 with root70/3/4, B100/5/6, T70/4/5, TB70/6/1.2, TT70/4/4. B costs $238.8M/yr and its BT product is comfortably on-spec (only 4% methylcyclopentane shown, zero cyclohexane), so 80/4/5 may retain the cut with meaningful energy/size savings. Root costs $268.2M and controls both C5/C6 cuts; do not weaken multiple linked splitters simultaneously. TT110/8/4 previously ruined both light products.

note: Restore the best plant and trim only the C6 splitter boil-up; the full-size column had 1% purity headroom, whereas smaller columns failed specification.
notebook:

Best: root70/3/4 dp.45; B100/5/6 dp.15; T70/4/5; TB70/6/1.2 dp.1; TT70/4/4. Revenue $1827.3M, cost $718.0M. BB naphthene recovery attempt failed badly. Root is $268.2M and controls linked C5/C6 recovery; avoid simultaneous changes.

notebook:

TBT and TTT are unsold; no need to purify them. TB is near C5 specification and should remain fixed. Root $268M controls both valuable blends; avoid until cheap columns are optimized.

notebook:
